findings.evidence: Plan structure: Overview, Prerequisites, Phases with tasks, Testing Strategy, Dependency Graph, Risks, Rollback ... Tasks must be small and independently testable
findings.fix: Cut the generic planning advice to a single line naming the required per-task fields (Location, Dependencies, Complexity, Acceptance Criteria). Spend the saved lines on Codex-specific facts the model would otherwise get wrong.

findings.evidence: When the plan arrives, check that every confirmed requirement maps to a task with acceptance criteria, list gaps, and do not implement unless asked.
findings.fix: Make plan review its own numbered step 6 with a fixed output: a requirement-to-task table, then missing or untestable criteria, then dependency cycles. Right now it is buried in a prose paragraph after the workflow ends.

findings.evidence: Never tell Codex to run tests or install packages: under `-s workspace-write` the network is off and the run stalls or fails.
findings.fix: Split the reason in two. Package installs and other network calls fail because the sandbox has no network. Running tests is only a problem when the tests need the network or the run takes too long. The real rule: a planning run should read files and write the plan, not execute the project.

findings.evidence: description: Prepare prompt_to_codex.md so the user can run Codex themselves and get an implementation plan in codex-plan.md. Use when planning a feature, API, auth change, migration or test strategy...
findings.fix: Prepare prompt_to_codex.md so the user can run OpenAI Codex CLI (codex exec) themselves and get an implementation plan in codex-plan.md. Use when the user wants to plan a feature, API, auth change, migration or test strategy with Codex, hand planning off to Codex, or write a Codex prompt, including underspecified requests. Gathers repo context, asks only blocking questions, shows the manual command. Not for implementing changes; never runs Codex.

findings.evidence: **Context first.** Read what the plan depends on.
findings.fix: Give context gathering a default scope, for example: manifest files, the entry points and modules the request names, and .env.example. Read more only when the request crosses module boundaries, so large repos do not trigger unbounded reading.

Add a branch for an empty `$ARGUMENTS` or one that contains only `--model <id>`. In that case, ask for the planning topic with AskUserQuestion before step 1, and never build a prompt with no objective.

findings.evidence: If either exists, ask whether to overwrite or use a numeric suffix
findings.fix: Check for existing output files before the readiness gate and put the overwrite-or-suffix question in the same AskUserQuestion batch. Step 2 says to ask in one batch, and step 3 currently forces a second round of questions.
